work.title: De Regibus Apostaticis

paragraphs.text: You have made it your habit to say that, unless your faith were sound and what you are doing to us were pleasing to God, you would already have been destroyed. So I have wished to lay before you what was done by a few kings who were your equals in apostasy and cruelty, so that this saying of yours may be buried: "If the faith of Arius, that is, my faith, were not catholic, and if it were not pleasing to God that I persecute the faith they wrote against us at Nicaea, I would certainly not still be flourishing in power." I do not mention kings who were strangers to the knowledge of God. I deal only with those who are known to have reigned in Judaea. In the book of Judges we find that Jerubbaal son of Joash was chosen by God and told: "Go in this strength of yours, and you will save Israel from the hand of Midian. Behold, am I not sending you?" And further on: "I will be with you, and you will strike Midian as if it were one man." Yet Scripture says this Midian had a multitude like the sand of the sea. But when everything God had promised Gideon was fulfilled, when he saw himself raised from lowliness, made rich from poverty, made a king from a commoner, what did he do at once? He said to the people: "Give me, each of you, an earring from his spoil." He received golden earrings weighing up to one thousand seven hundred shekels, besides the bracelets, necklaces, coverings and purple that the kings of Midian had worn, and besides the golden chains that hung on the necks of the enemy's camels. And what does holy Scripture say Gideon did then? "And Gideon made them into an ephod and set it up in his city Ophrah. And the children of Israel went whoring after it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and his house." Did he wait even a few days before doing this wicked work against God? When he set about it, could he not remember that God had said to him, "Go, I will be with you"? What became of the fact that he had demolished Baal at God's command, cut down his groves and offered sacrifice to God? What became of what he had said to God's messenger when the messenger told him, "The Lord is with you, mighty in strength"? He had answered: "I pray, my lord, if the Lord is with us, why have all these evils seized us? And where are his wonders, which our fathers told us of, saying: Did not God bring us out of Egypt? And now the Lord has spurned us and handed us over into the hand of Midian." When he set out to act against God, did he not call to mind that those evils had come on them because of idolatry? Yet once they had been rescued, so that they could live without fear of their enemies, from all the evils that he said had weighed on him and all the people, he immediately did the very thing that would get both himself and the whole people handed over to their enemies again for idolatry. He had heard from God that all those evils had befallen them because they forsook God and served idols. He remembered what the prophet had said. And yet on the very day their enemies were brought to nothing before them, that king, whom you are pleased to resemble, decided in his madness that idols should be served rather than the God who had given him all this. "And the children of Israel," says Scripture, "did evil before the Lord God, and he handed them over into the hands of Midian for seven years, and the hand of Midian prevailed greatly over Israel. And because of Midian the Israelites made themselves hiding places in the mountains, and caves and strongholds. And whenever Israel sowed, Midian and Amalek and the people of the East would come up. They came up against them and fought with them and ruined the land as far as Gaza, and they left Israel nothing to live on, neither sheep nor calf nor ass. For they came up with their cattle, and brought their tents and led their camels, and came like locusts in multitude, for they were without number, and they came upon the land to ruin it. And Israel was made poor before Midian. And the children of Israel cried to the Lord. And because the children of Israel cried to the Lord on account of Midian, the Lord sent a prophet to the children of Israel, and he said to them: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: I am he who brought you up from Egypt and led you out of the house of slavery, and took you from the hand of the king of Egypt and from the hand of all who persecuted you. I drove them out before you and gave you their land. And I said to you: I am the Lord your God. Do not fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell. But you did not listen to my voice." After this rebuke from the Lord, what does Jerubbaal, who is also called Gideon, do? As soon as he sees his enemy brought to nothing, as soon as all those adversaries are slaughtered (adversaries said to have been like the sand of the sea, and slaughtered not by a vast number of Israelites but by three hundred men), as soon as he sees all the foreign kings slain, he fashions the very thing through which the children of Israel would sin against God. And yet we find that he reigned in Israel for forty years even after committing so great a crime. So it will be no surprise if you too, sacrilegious as you are, still live on in the body, when you see that King Gideon lived forty years after committing idolatry and kept his kingdom. For holy Scripture says that the Israelites had rest for forty years, that no enemies at all were allowed against them and no foreigner ruled over them, because they had cried out to God. Such were the benefits God bestowed on your partners in sacrilege. He showed that he is indeed all-powerful, but he also showed that they were unworthy to obtain rest, since after receiving rest from such great dangers they would not choose to serve, for even a single day, the one who had shown them such great mercy. The Israelites were like this, and yet in his goodness he spared them even when they practised idolatry afterwards. He did not repay them at once. But in his own time he did repay them, for the guilt of idolatry could not go unpunished. So he will repay you too, Constantius, unless you look to yourself in the meantime. The Israelites served demons and forsook God, and had already become strangers to the knowledge of God. Yet as soon as it entered their hearts that the almighty God is the one who had led their fathers out of the land of Egypt, they were heard and freed from the hand of Midian and from all who persecuted them. What, then, do you suppose we Christians may expect: to be rescued from your hands? Or do you deny, and fail to see, as far as I know, that we worship none other than the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and of all the prophets, apostles and martyrs? Believe me, we have been heard and we will be heard, so that you, with all your fragile grandeur, may lie beneath the heel of all his servants. And if there is some delay, so that he does not yet destroy you Arians and give his holy church the full security of peace, the reason is this: it is fitting that, while you rage against us as an adversary, all should be brought to their testing.

You say: "If I had done wrong, if I held a heresy, God would already have taken vengeance on me." Yet you hear holy Scripture telling how the Lord spared even foreign peoples for a long time, and how they afterwards received what their deeds deserved. Samuel said to Saul: "The Lord sent me to anoint you king over Israel. Now hear the voice of the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord Almighty: Now I will avenge what Amalek did to you, Israel, how he met you on the way when you came up from Egypt. Now go and strike Amalek and all that is his, and do not covet anything of theirs. Wipe him out and put him under the ban, him and all that is his. Do not spare him, but kill everything of his, man and woman, infant and nursing child." And further on: "And Saul came to the city of Amalek, and drew near and lay in wait for Amalek in the valley. And Saul said to the Kenite: Go, withdraw from among them and turn aside from Amalek. Do not join yourself to him, for you showed mercy to the children of Israel when they came up out of Egypt. And the Kenite withdrew from among Amalek, and Saul struck Amalek from Havilah as far as Shur, which faces Egypt. And Saul took Agag king of Amalek alive, and killed all his people with the edge of the sword." You see how, though late, they received the reward of their crime. And you say: "If I were not acting rightly, I would never reign for long." We find that Saul himself was rejected for acting against the Lord's command, and yet he reigned a long time after his rejection, after God had said to Samuel: "I regret that I anointed Saul king." And you say: "If my belief were not right, if I did not live in a way pleasing to God, I would certainly not still be ruling now." So that you may take in fully what we are saying about Saul, hear what he did against the Lord's command: "And Saul and all his people took Agag the king, and the best of the flocks and herds, of the food and the vineyards and of all good things. They would not destroy all the good things, but kept back every precious piece of work and destroyed what was worthless. And the word of the Lord came to Samuel, saying: I regret that I made Saul king, for he has turned away from me and has not carried out my words. And Samuel was grieved and cried to God all night, and before daylight Samuel went out to meet Israel." And further on: "And Samuel came to Saul, and behold, Saul was offering a burnt offering to the Lord, the first of the spoils he had brought from Amalek. And Samuel reached Saul, and Saul said to him: Blessed are you by the Lord. I have carried out everything the Lord said. And Samuel said: Then what is this sound of the flock in my ears, and the sound of oxen that I hear? And Saul said: I brought them from Amalek. The people took as spoil the best of the flock and of the oxen, to be sacrificed to the Lord your God. The rest I destroyed and wiped out. And Samuel said to Saul: Were you not the least in your own sight, the leader of the tribes from among Israel? And the Lord anointed you king over Israel, and the Lord sent you on your way and said to you: Go and destroy Amalek, those who sin against me, and fight against them until you have consumed them. Why then did you not obey the voice of the Lord, but swooped upon the spoil and did what is evil in the Lord's sight? And Saul said: Because I listened to the people. I went on the way on which God sent me, and I brought back Agag king of Amalek, and I destroyed Amalek. And the people took from the spoil the flock and the choicest of the herds of those I destroyed, to sacrifice before the Lord our God in Gilgal. And Samuel said: Does the Lord want burnt offerings and sacrifices more than obedience to the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to heed is better than the fat of rams. For sin is an abomination; you have brought pains and groans upon yourself. Because you counted the word of the Lord as nothing, the Lord will count you as nothing, so that you shall not reign. And Saul said to Samuel: I have sinned, for I have transgressed the word of the Lord and your word, because I feared the people and listened to their voice. Now take away my sin and come back with me, and I will worship the Lord your God. And Samuel said to him: This day the Lord will tear your kingdom over Israel from your hand and give it to your neighbour, who is better than you." And further on: "And Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death, for Samuel mourned over Saul, and the Lord regretted that he had made Saul king over Israel. And the Lord said to Samuel: How long will you mourn over Saul? Behold, I am casting him out so that he shall not reign over Israel. Fill your horn with oil and come; I will send you to Jesse in Bethlehem, for I have heard of a king for myself among the sons of Jesse." Now, Constantius, you can see that even those rejected by the Lord, even those destined for eternal death, may reign for a long time after committing a grave offence. You see that after David, the glorious son of Jesse, was anointed king, Saul still reigned a long time and even had power to persecute the man God had chosen for himself as prophet and king. The wicked man persecuted the good, the unjust the just, the one hateful to God the one God loved. Since this is so, do not boast that you have lived on until now after so great a crime, as Saul did. Consider instead what kind of punishment came upon Saul, for it can come upon you too unless you take thought for yourself. If the Lord was so angry with him, first for taking spoil against God's prohibition and second for persecuting David, God's own man, how much more must the punishment of his anger fall on you, whose crimes are so enormous that you have even incurred the guilt of sacrilege.

"If I had done wrong," you say, "if I were a heretic, as Lucifer says, God would already have taken the kingdom from me." Learn, then, that Solomon too lived on after committing idolatry, and be pleased to understand that you are just what he was after his idolatry. "And the Lord raised up an adversary against Solomon, Hadad the Edomite, and Rezon son of Eliada in Bemathad [?], Hadadezer king of Zobah his lord. And men gathered to him, and he was leader of the band, and he seized the city of Damascus and settled in it and reigned in Damascus. And they were adversaries to Solomon and to Israel all the days of Solomon." We have shown you that Solomon too reigned for some years after his idolatry, when he was certainly serving no longer God but the devil, which is why he is described as having clung to men of the devil. In the same way you cling to your partners in sacrilege, the Arians. Though you are still in the body, and though you still keep your throne, you are found to be just what Solomon was after he forsook God and followed idols. You wanted us to cling to the kind of men that Solomon made the Israelites cling to. Where was that love of God which the holy Scriptures say Solomon had, at the time when he saw fit to follow idols and forsake God? How did this come about, unless he had become a man wholly estranged from sober understanding? I do not want you to congratulate yourself that, though you are a blasphemer and a destroyer of God's religion, you still hold the kingdom and carry yourself proudly after your sacrilege. For we find that Rehoboam son of Solomon also practised idolatry and lived on in his kingship for twenty years. Holy Scripture says of him: "And King Solomon slept with his fathers in the city of David, and his son Rehoboam reigned in his place in Jerusalem. He was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty years in Jerusalem." And further on: "And he did evil in the sight of the Lord and did not walk in the way of his father David." Solomon, from the time he saw fit to enslave himself to idols, and his son Rehoboam, who served idols all his life, did not walk in David's paths, and yet both lived on in their kingship and both reached the last day of their lives still reigning. Why then do you marvel that, after committing your crime and living on in that wickedness, you still sit proudly as king, and that God takes neither your kingdom nor your life from you? You see that Jeroboam, too, tried as you do to overturn the Lord's religion from its foundations, and yet lived on for a great many years while persisting in that wickedness, as it is written: "And there was a man from Mount Ephraim, a servant of Solomon, and his name was Jeroboam, and his mother's name was Sarira, a harlot." And in another place: "And when all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned from Egypt, they sent and called him to the assembly and made him king over Israel." And further on: "And Jeroboam said in his heart: Now the kingdom will return to David. If this people goes up to offer sacrifice in the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, the heart of the people will turn back to their lord Rehoboam king of Judah. So Jeroboam took counsel, and went and made two golden heifers, and said to the people: Enough of your going up to Jerusalem. Here are your gods, Israel, who brought you back from the land of Egypt. And he set up one in Bethel and put the other in Dan. And this thing became a sin, and the people went before the one heifer as far as Dan. And they built houses on the high places, and he made priests from some part of the people who were not of the sons of Levi. And Jeroboam held a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth of the month, like the feast in Judah, and went up to the sanctuary he had made in Bethel to sacrifice before the heifers he had made. And he appointed in Bethel priests of the high places he had made. And he went up to the sanctuary he had made, on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, at the feast he had devised in his own heart, and he held a feast for the children of Israel."

So do not boast that you still live and possess the glory of kingship while you practise idolatry. You see that this Jeroboam made golden heifers and turned the people of Israel to idolatry, and yet he was not only not destroyed the moment he sinned but was even allowed to live a long time. Could God not have removed those idolatrous kings? But it has been shown how ungrateful to God you are, you who, though so highly exalted, not only forget the one who exalts you but go on persecuting him in his servants, wanting to remove his religion altogether. You can see that this is so from what this king Jeroboam did. He was the son of a slave woman and remembered that he was born of a harlot. He received the kingdom of his lord Solomon, to that same Solomon's disgrace. Why then did he forsake God and turn to idols? Jeroboam knew, I say, that the kingdom had been given him by God because his lord Solomon had followed idols. Yet he counted all this as nothing and resolved to make idols, and to enslave himself to them, together with all the people who served God, rather than to the living God, who had made him, the son of a harlot, master of his lord Solomon's kingdom. So do not wonder that God spares you, ungrateful men who sin against him. Rather, I urge you to see that, though late, if you persist in this wickedness of yours, you will receive what all your predecessors in sacrilege received. We urge you to be pleased to rescue yourself from such great evils. Moreover, you have <examples>: you are not the first to do this. We see that this same Jeroboam counted the Lord's warning as nothing. "And at that time," it says, "Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, and Ahijah the Shilonite, the prophet, found him on the road. Ahijah was dressed in a new garment, and the two of them were alone in the field. And Ahijah took hold of the new garment he was wearing and tore it into twelve pieces, and said to Jeroboam: Take ten pieces for yourself, for thus says the Lord God of Israel: Behold, I am tearing the kingdom out of Solomon's hand, and I will give you ten tribes. Two tribes shall remain his for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of the city of Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel. For Solomon has forsaken me and made Astarte, the unclean idol of the Sidonians, and Chemosh, the idol of Moab, and their king, the object of worship of the children of Ammon, and he has not walked in my ways to do what is right before me, as his father David did. But I will not take the whole kingdom out of his hand during his lifetime, for the sake of my servant David whom I chose, though I will set myself against him all the days of his life. I will take the kingdom out of his son's hand and give you ten tribes, and to his son I will give two tribes, so that my servant David may always have a place before me in Jerusalem, the city I have chosen for myself to put my name there. And I will take you, and you shall reign over whatever your soul desires, and you shall be king over Israel. And if you keep all that I command you, and walk in my ways, and do what is right in my sight, and keep my precepts and my commandments as my servant David did, I will be with you and build you a sure house, as I built for David." Here was a man born of a harlot, a man who remembered that he came of slave stock, and he heard these things from God. Once everything the Lord had promised was fulfilled, did he obey the one who had promised him so much? Did he not, as soon as he saw himself exalted, set out to act against him? Did not Jeroboam at once set to work so that God would be forsaken by all his worshippers?

We tell you that unless you correct yourself, unless you begin to walk in the ways that please God, you will perish and become a fresh example; and still you remain in your iniquity and persist in your sacrilege. This is nothing new. God had the things already mentioned brought to this King Jeroboam through his man; and when Jeroboam's son was held fast by a grave illness, the king sent to God's servant and heard what was to come. Yet even when he saw the evils foretold to him being fulfilled, he acted more and more against God and wanted God's house destroyed. "There was a man from Shiloh," Scripture says, "named Ahijah, and he was sixty years old, and the word of the Lord was with him. And Jeroboam said to his wife: Get up, and take in your hand loaves for the man of God, and cakes for his children, and grapes, and a jar of honey. And the woman got up and did as her husband had told her. Now Ahijah was a very old man, and his eyes were too dim to see. And the woman set out from Baria and went. And when she had entered the city to Ahijah the Shilonite, Ahijah said to his servant: Go out now to meet Anna, the wife of Jeroboam, and say to her: Come in and do not stand there, for thus says the Lord: I am sending hard things upon you. And Anna went in to the man of God, and Ahijah said to her: Why have you brought me loaves and grapes and cakes and a jar of honey? Thus says the Lord: See, you will go away from me, and when you enter the gate of the city of Arira, your maidservants will come out to meet you and say to you: The boy is dead. For thus says the Lord: See, I will destroy every male of this Jeroboam, everyone who urinates against the wall; and those of Jeroboam's who die in the city the dogs will eat, and those of his who die in the field the birds of the sky will eat." It is nothing new, I say, if you stand firm in this stubbornness, since you know that this Jeroboam was not deterred by any of these things. For at once, just as the man of God had said, as soon as the woman entered the city their son died. And yet Jeroboam did not see what God would bring upon him for having forsaken him and for having made the people perish along with him. Nor did the death of his son make him afraid that the rest might follow; instead he grew old in his cunning. Indeed, from the time he departed from the one who had handed the kingdom to him, Jeroboam had become so bereft of his senses that, though he had said, "Go to the man of God and learn whether our son is to die," and had learned through the man of God that not only would their son die but dangers hung over his whole kingdom, he still chose, as he had resolved once and for all, to serve the devil. He sends to the man of God to ask about the future, and yet he spurns the very one whose man he sends to; to insult his majesty he makes calves and makes the people worship them along with him. This is what he did, and yet he was not destroyed on the spot, but survived long in his kingdom. And you say: "If I were a heretic, if I were attacking God's religion, as Lucifer, Pancratius and Hilary say, vengeance would already have been taken on me." Hear further what happened to this King Jeroboam, and how even so he was not converted to God, but rather died persisting in his crime and perished in his sacrilege: "And Jeroboam held a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like the feast of Judah, and he went up to the sacrifice that he had made in Bethel, to sacrifice to the calves that he had made; and he appointed in Bethel priests of the high places that he had made. And he went up to the altar that he had made, on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, at the feast that he had devised out of his own heart, and he held a feast for the children of Israel and went up to the altar to sacrifice. And behold, a man of God came from Judah to Bethel by the word of the Lord, while Jeroboam was standing at his altar to sacrifice; and the prophet cried out against the altar by the word of the Lord, saying: O altar, altar, thus says the Lord: Behold, a son will be born to the house of David, and Josiah will be his name, and he will sacrifice upon you the priests of the high places who sacrifice upon you, and he will burn human bones upon you. And on that day he will give a sign which the Lord has spoken: Behold, the altar will be split apart and the fat that is on it will be poured out. And when the king heard the words of the man of God who cried out against the altar that was in Bethel, he stretched out his hand toward the altar, saying: Seize him! And the king's hand, which he had stretched out against him, withered, and he could not draw it back to himself. And the sacrifice burst apart, and its fat was poured out from the altar, according to the sign that the man of God had given by the word of the Lord. And the king answered and said to the man of God: Entreat the face of the Lord your God, that my hand may be restored to me. And the man of God entreated the face of the Lord, and the king's hand was restored to him and became as it was before." When he had seen the signs fulfilled that had been uttered by the mouth of the man of God, and his impious arm, stretched out to kill the man of God, suddenly withered for fear, and then at once restored whole through the prayer of God's worshipper, did he do away with the idolatry he himself had set up? Did he at last abolish the feast he himself had devised out of his own heart? Not at all; rather, he is found to have met the day of his death in that same stubbornness of presumption. So we will hardly be able to wonder if—God forbid it for you—you resolve to meet the day of your death in your heresy, since even signs and wonders could not call your fellow sacrilegists of old back to the worship of the one God. For holy Scripture says of Jeroboam: "And after this Jeroboam did not turn back from his wickedness, but again made priests of the high places from among the people. Whoever wished raised his hand and became a priest of the high places. And this thing became sin to the house of Jeroboam, and its ruin and its destruction from the face of the earth."

So that these things may not be said of you as well, I beg you to rescue yourself from the abominable company of the Arians. I beg you to become a Christian again, as you were before, instead of an Arian. And do not be indignant with us for setting your deeds side by side with Jeroboam's. Rather, I implore you to see that I am pressing all these things on you for the good of your salvation, and that they should be called instructions rather than rebukes. For we compare you to Jeroboam because in our times you have tried to turn everyone away from God, just as he tried to make the people of Israel apostates instead of worshippers of God. Do not go on promising yourself any hope from the fact that you do evil and yet still reign. You see that Jeroboam reigned a long time in his wickedness; and so did Solomon's son, who also practiced idolatry and died in that same wickedness; and likewise his son Abijah, of whom I find it written: "And he walked in the sins of his father, which he had committed before him, and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as the heart of David his father had been." Yet although they served idols, they held the kingdom, died in that high rank, and handed the authority of the kingdom on to their sons. So do not congratulate yourself on this either: that your father handed the kingdom on to you, so that you say: "Had my father not done well to join the Arians, we his sons would never be reigning." Do not say: "If I were a heretic, I would never wield such power; God would never still allow me to be on the throne." For you see that Baasha son of Ahijah reigned over Israel for twenty-four years, of whom you have found it written in the third book of Kingdoms: "And he did evil before the Lord and walked in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sins, with which he made Israel sin." King Baasha certainly ought to have feared being struck down like Jeroboam if he departed from the ways of the Lord. But you who turn aside from God are such that, once it has pleased you to take up the service of idolatry as an insult to God, not even the example of those already judged can frighten you into turning to God. It is also written of King Omri: "And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, and did worse than all who were before him, and walked in all the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sins." And yet this man, who is said to have sinned beyond all the kings before him, was not destroyed the moment he forsook God. Nor was he afflicted with any grave illness, so that he who is described as having sinned more gravely might be seen to be destroyed by a heavier punishment. You see, Constantius, that even if it is your lot to spend this temporal life in the greatest prosperity, you ought to be all the more afraid, because you are being reserved for God's judgment. Granted, those who are destroyed at once, on whom some punishment is inflicted by God here, are still always tormented after they go down. Yet if you are snatched away from here while living in the greatest prosperity, consider how vengeance will proceed against you, who are found in so great a crime. So do not count it as any good fortune that, though you deny the only Son of God and persecute his household, your spirit still remains in that executioner's body of yours. Consider that the son of Asa, a man as sacrilegious as you, reigned among the Jews for thirty-five years, and you have read that it is written of him: "He walked in the ways of Asa his father and did not turn aside from them, so as to do what was right in the sight of the Lord; but they did not keep away from the high places, and they sacrificed and burned incense on the high places." See, here too the king is described as having fallen asleep in peace. So since he practiced idolatry for thirty-five years, do not take it as a credit to yourself and say: "This is why I am not wounded by any blow, this is why I have not yet been destroyed but still live in possession of the rule of the Roman Empire: because I believe rightly; because Arius's faith is right; because I have done well to remove bishops and to install others of the kind Arius would have wished." Do not, I say, boast of this, nor be proud that you go on doing these things, when you see that this king held his throne for thirty-five years and was taken away in peace. If, then, because they were taken away in that manner, the crime of idolatry could go unpunished for them, it can go unpunished for you too, Constantius! Turn, therefore, to the Lord, so that you may not be found to be such as Ahab was found to be, of whom I find it written: "And Ahab did evil in the sight of the Lord, and did worse than all who were before him. And it was not enough for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, but he also took as his wife Jezebel, daughter of Basan and Hela [?], king of the Sidonians. And he went and served Baal and worshipped him, and set up an altar to Baal in the house of his cults, which he built in Samaria. And Ahab made a sacred grove, to provoke, to provoke God to anger and destroy his own soul; and he did worse than all the kings of Israel who were before him." Do not let yourself remain any longer among the Arians, but cross over to us Christians, for whom all heresies are what Baal was. You heretics are now to us what those who sacrificed to idols were to the worshippers of God in those times. Believe me: through this heresy of yours you are in our times what Ahab was in his.

So do not be pleased with yourself that God has not repaid you at once. You see that this Ahab and his wife Jezebel were spared for a very long time, though they even killed the prophets of the Lord and are found to have been steeped in such crime that they let no one who confessed himself a man of God remain in the land of Israel. Do not fix your eyes on the fact that you do evil and yet still swagger in your crimes. Rather, I beseech you, see this: unless you are converted, then just as the reward of their works was paid back to them, however late, so it can be brought upon you as well. Do not say: "This is why I have long been on the throne, this is why I am powerful: because I hold the good faith, because I do right in persecuting those who believe as that faith set down at Nicaea holds." Do not, I say, say these things. Instead, I pray you, see this: you are left in your pride after so many killings of yours for one purpose, that either you listen to us, God's priests, and turn to God, or else you receive what your deeds deserve at a time when you will not be able to say that you erred in ignorance. Take warning from the example of Ahab, the slayer of the Lord's prophets and worshipper of all the demons, and see that this is so. Understand that this man, so wicked, was kept on the throne for a long time after such great crimes so that at last, if he wished, he might be converted. Not only was he not paid back for his evil deeds, he was even helped in his difficulties, no doubt so that he could infer that he had been rescued not by Baal and the other demons, whom the heathen call gods, but by the God of Israel, whose prophet he saw speaking with him and declaring to him how God would bring the enemies of the Israelites to nothing. For Ben-hadad the king had besieged Samaria with thirty-two other kings, boasting that he counted the Israelites as so utterly nothing that he, one man, would overcome the whole multitude of the Israelites. God made this foreigner as nothing before Israel. For which king did God win the victory? For Ahab, of course, the very man who had forsaken him, who had made Israel serve Baal and all the demons. God helped him for this reason: that he might believe that the only God is the one whose people Israel was, and that there is no other besides him who had won the victory for him; so that Ahab might see that it was right for him at last to correct his errors. As soon as the enemy began to lay siege to the Israelites' city, "behold," says holy Scripture, "a prophet came to the king of Israel and said: Thus says the Lord: Have you heard this great noise? Behold, today I will deliver it into your hands, and you will know that I am the Lord. And the king said: By whom? And the prophet said: By the young men of the governors of the districts. And the king said: Who will begin the battle? And the prophet said: You." And further on: "And the young men of the governors of the districts went out of the city, and the army after them, and each struck down the man he found beside him, and the Syrians fled, and Israel pursued them." How can you say, Constantius: "If I were not serving God well, if I did not believe rightly, I would never have seen the Roman Empire placed in my power, nor would I have lived so long on the throne"? For you see that to Ahab, king of Israel—who lived in the manner of the Gentiles and turned the people of God away from God, just as you do—it was said by the very one against whom he was sinning and whose commands he counted for nothing: "I deliver it into your hands, that you may know that I am God." As, then, he rescued Ahab from Ben-hadad, king of Syria, so too he has rescued and still rescues you from all who seek to destroy you, surely so that you may recognize that he is the God of the patriarchs and the martyrs, and so that you may infer that victory has been granted you not because of the merits of your faith and your life—since you are like King Ahab in every respect—but that mercy has been shown you, against your merits, by the one you have forsaken, just as it was shown to Ahab. For if you say that you defeat your enemies because you believe rightly, Ahab too, the worshipper of idols and slayer of the holy prophets, could have said the same. Do you not see, then, that you have been preserved so that you might correct your errors? The moment you took possession of Italy, you tried to overturn its church. You said that God the Father is not truly God the Father, denying his only Son and asserting that he is not truly the Son. You even maintained that the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, was made out of nothing. You tried to defend the claim that there was a time when the only Son of God did not exist. You devoted all your strength to doing away, if you could, with the apostolic and evangelical tradition. By your authority you had bishops removed who had been ordained by God's judgment, and you saw to it that heretics were installed in their places who could preach your heresy. You fought against the church in Alexandria with military force; you banished a great many bishops into exile and to the mines, you threw them into prison, and you even killed a certain number of all the worshippers of God. Though you have done these things, you still say: "Unless I were doing well and believing soundly, God would never still let me reign"—as though God had been patient with Ahab and your other fellow idolaters because they held to the right way. So, because God in his tireless kindness is patient with your sins, as he was with King Ahab, you think that you are not sinning but are being spared because of your merits. You imitate Ahab in this too: you love those who give you evil counsel and destroy those who tell you the truth for the sake of your salvation. Those four hundred false prophets told Ahab that he would meet with every success, while Micaiah, the prophet of God, said the opposite, that every evil would befall him; and Ahab loved those false prophets more than the true prophet of the Lord. In the same way you love your fellow heretics the Arians and obey what they say, while you curse all of us priests of the Lord: first of all, because we confess the Son of God to be the true Son of God; secondly, because we do not flatter you, because we insist that you are in danger, and because we say that unless you turn to God you will come to eternal punishment.

So that you may believe that apostate men have always hated the men of God, and loved the enemies of God's religion, that is, the worshippers of the devil, learn whom Ahab loved and whom he hated. "And Jehoshaphat king of Judah said to the king of Israel: Inquire of the Lord today. And the king of Israel called together all the prophets, about four hundred men, and King Ahab said to them: Shall I go to battle at Ramoth-gilead, or shall I refrain? And they said: Go up." And further on: "And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel: Is there no prophet of the Lord here, that we may inquire of the Lord? And Ahab king of Israel said to King Jehoshaphat: There is one man through whom we may inquire of the Lord, but I hate him, because he speaks nothing good about me." Again, after Micaiah the Lord's prophet had told him not to go up, since if he went up he would not return: "The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah: Did I not tell you that this man prophesies nothing good for me, but only evil?" To that senseless man, whom the devil had already taken hold of, the things spoken by God's servant seemed evil, and the things spoken by the devil's servants were judged good. It is no wonder, then, that Ahab listened to those the devil made him listen to, his own slaves, of course, and refused to listen to those whom God showed to be his servants, both by their endurance of suffering and by the steadfastness of their testimony. The false prophets were sent away by the king enriched and honored, but Micaiah, the Lord's prophet, is shut up in prison, and it is said: "Let him eat the bread of affliction until I return." And yet, just as the servant of God had said, he did not return at all. You act the same way, Constantius. You love those who drag you along with them to everlasting death, who lead your soul to utter destruction, and in return you see fit to hate those who long for you to become a friend of God. Do not boast that, though you do such things, you still hold on to this fragile life, mighty in the glory of kingship. The sacred scriptures tell us that Jeroboam son of Joash also reigned over Israel in Samaria for forty-one years, and did so while serving idols, having forsaken God, and never departing from the wickedness of Ahab king of Israel and the sacrifices of Jeroboam. "If I had done wrong," you say, "God would have removed me from the throne long ago." As if the son of Amaziah, because he did not turn away from vain things, was not struck with leprosy, and yet reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem! But you outdo King Uzziah in this: you do not have the elephantiasis that could eat away all your limbs, but the kind that can defile the soul through and through. Grieve for yourself with us and shed tears for yourself. Look how this visible elephantiasis defiles the body, how the poison of leprosy eats away the limbs. Understand that the Arian heresy, your elephantiasis, defiles everything within you in the same way. Observe that it makes your inner man just like those you see covered with elephantiasis, whom this disease has seized. Do not say: "If I were not acting well, I would never have ruled so long, I would never have been allowed to live until now," when you see that Manasseh too, son of King Hezekiah and king of Judah, took the throne at sixteen years of age and reigned fifty-seven years. When you hear what is written about him, you will surely find that you are his imitator. Then you will no longer wonder that, though you do evil, you are still spared, seeing that Manasseh, whom you match in cruelty and sacrilege, held the kingdom for fifty-seven years while doing such things. "And Hezekiah slept with his fathers," says scripture, "and was buried in the city of David, and Manasseh his son reigned in his place. Manasseh was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-seven years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Hephzibah. And he did what is evil in the sight of the Lord, according to the abominations of the nations whom the Lord drove out before the children of Israel. He rebuilt the high places which his father Hezekiah had destroyed, built a shrine to Baal, and made sacred groves as Ahab king of Israel had done, and he worshipped all the host of heaven and served them. He built a shrine in the two courts of the house of the Lord, made his sons pass into the fire, practiced augury, and appointed many mediums and diviners, so as to do what is evil in the eyes of his soul, so as to provoke the Lord God. He made carved images of the groves and set them in the house of which the Lord had said to David and to Solomon his son: In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name forever; and I will no longer make the foot of Israel wander from the land which I gave them, if only they listen to me in all that I have commanded them, and according to the law which my servant Moses commanded them. But they did not listen. Manasseh utterly scorned the Lord and led them astray, so that they did more evil than all the nations which the Lord removed from before Israel. And the Lord spoke by the hand of his servants the prophets: Because of the idols which Manasseh king of Judah has made, according to all that the Amorites did who were before him, and because he has made Judah sin with his idols, therefore thus says the Lord God of Israel: Behold, I am bringing evils upon Jerusalem and Judah, so that both ears of everyone who hears of it will ring. I will stretch over Jerusalem the measuring line of Samaria and the plummet of the house of Ahab, and I will wipe out Jerusalem as a boxwood tablet is wiped clean from the doorpost before his face. I will give them into the hands of their enemies, and they will become plunder and fuel for burning to all their enemies, because they have turned away from following me and have been provoking me from the day their fathers came out of the land of Egypt until this day. Now the rest of the words of Manasseh and all that he did, how he made Israel sin, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? And he shed a great deal of innocent blood, until he filled Jerusalem from end to end, besides the sin by which he made Judah sin, so as to do what is evil in the sight of the Lord God. And Manasseh slept with his fathers, and his son Amon reigned in his place, being twenty-two years old."

What do you say to this, Constantius? I believe you will now stop saying, "If I were not acting well, I would not have reigned so long," when you see that this other man, Manasseh, did such things and reigned fifty-seven years. And since we have said that you are another Manasseh, see how you share all his traits. He set up idolatry in the house of God; you have done just as much in the temple and courts of the Lord. He had idols worshipped and seized for himself what was called the Lord's, so that from then on it could be called the idols'. You have done all this too, because you brought the Arian heresy into the church, and you who decreed that your blasphemy be received as the catholic faith command that the faith written at Nicaea, which we know to be apostolic and evangelical, be spat upon. Just as you now have longed for these things to be done, so Manasseh commanded that all the idols be served and God abandoned. It will be no surprise, then, if you have claimed for yourself the buildings in which we used to gather God's people, and, though an idolater, have called yourself catholic, when you see that Manasseh did what you have now done. So in the end the Lord will spare you too, as you keep to Manasseh's way, just as he spared him and for as long as he spared him: it is written that he slept with his fathers and was buried in Jerusalem and that his son took up the kingdom in his place. Do you read that he perished in war or was struck down by some illness? Not at all. But what do you make of it? I suppose, in that wisdom of yours, you say that King Manasseh got away with all of it unpunished. You are the sort of man to think this of Manasseh: that because he reigned fifty-seven years, handed the kingdom to his son, and died in peace himself, such great crimes could have gone unpunished. Do not take pity on yourself by turning to God, do not correct your wicked deeds, and you will find yourself in torment with Manasseh, whom you plainly surpass in this: he shed the blood of the righteous only within the bounds of Jerusalem, while you have shed it and still shed it throughout the whole Roman realm. "But," you say, "he burned or consecrated his sons before the images of his gods." If you had had sons, you would no doubt have made them accept the Arian blasphemy. Or do you not know that, just as those who burned their sons pleased the devil then, since they were of one mind to forsake the Creator and serve the creature, so now the devil demands nothing of you except that you deny the only Son of God? This is the sacrifice most acceptable to him: that you believe as Arius believed. In our times it is worth more to him that you deny the Son of God than if you were willing to burn yourself in the fire in honor of all the demons. For he sees that the worship of idols is despised by everyone, since it was an empty invention. Now he wants to use you heretics, his servants, to deceive us, the servants of God. "How," you ask, "deceive?" Just as he has already deceived you, so he wants us to be deceived. Though you are an Arian, you pretend to be a Christian until you can wound the defenseless with the poison of your heresy, so that from then on they may no longer be Christians, as we are, but Arians, as you are. This is the rich offering of your services, which is presented through you to the demons. For who but the devil and his sons can say of the only Son of God: "He is a son and is not a true son; he is God and is not true God"? So when you say, "I am a Christian, but I do not believe that God has a true Son; I do not believe in one power of the Father and the Son"; when you call the Son a creature, made from nothing; when you say that there was a time when he was not, you sacrifice to the devil more pleasingly than Manasseh did when he consecrated his sons to all the demons by fire or burned them.

I grieve for you, emperor, that while you are so foolish and do such great evils, you still see fit to say: "If I were not acting well, I would not still be on the throne; God would already have destroyed me." Do you not see that this Manasseh, who is comparable to you in sacrilege and cruelty, held the kingdom in Judea for fifty-seven years, as I have often said? This is the very man who made the people forsake God and serve idols, who set up images in the temple of the Lord and the courts of God, who turned the house of God, the sanctuary of his majesty, into a sanctuary of idols. In the same way God bears with you and puts up with you, until he has tested his own household, crowned the worthy, and, unless you correct yourself, punished the unworthy along with you with eternal punishment. For the rest, believe that he could have destroyed Manasseh then and you now in the twinkling of an eye. But he spares you, not because he cannot do otherwise, but because it is fitting both that his worshippers, standing unmoved against your cruelty, should be crowned, and that you, the enemies of his mercy, should be condemned by him to everlasting punishment, if you resolve to persist as you are. It is those around you who make you say, "If I were not acting well, I would never still be ruling"; they not only do not want you corrected in your error, but even drive you to your ruin. No wonder; for it is written that both you and they would be such: "The sinner is praised in the desires of his soul, and he who does wrong is blessed. The sinner has provoked the Lord; in the greatness of his wrath he will not seek him. God is not before his eyes; his ways are defiled at all times; his judgments are taken away from his sight." So when you say, "We do well to remove those bishops who confess that they hold the faith written at Nicaea, and to install those who confess as Arius confessed," and they say, "Quite right!", then surely you are that sinner who is wrongly praised for the desires of his soul. And you are that wrongdoer who, though abandoned by God for your blasphemies, is never rebuked by your flatterers for whatever wrong you do, but is told instead that you are acting well. When you say, "I did well to send soldiers to Alexandria to remove Athanasius," and they say, "Absolutely right!", to whom will you be compared, if not to the man the Holy Spirit marks out through the psalmist: the man who does wrong, who is utterly wicked and accursed, and yet longs to be praised? You say, "If I were not acting well, God would not have spared me until now." But I find these words addressed to God: "Therefore you correct little by little those who go astray, and you admonish and remind those who sin, so that they may abandon their wickedness and believe in you, O Lord. For you hated those ancient inhabitants of your land because they did works hateful to you, sorceries and unholy rites, and you willed to destroy those merciless murderers of children by the hands of our fathers, so that the land dearest to you of all might receive a worthy colony of the children of God. But even these, as being men, you spared, and you sent wasps as forerunners of your army to destroy them little by little. Were you unable to put the ungodly under the righteous in battle, or to destroy them all at once by savage beasts or by one stern word? But by judging them little by little you gave them room for repentance, though you knew that their race was wicked and their malice inborn, and that their way of thinking would never change; for they were a seed accursed from the beginning. Nor was it out of fear of anyone that you granted pardon for their sins. For who will say to you, What have you done? Or who will stand against your judgment?"

In the same way you too are being spared, Constantius, so that you may repent, or else perish after the example of those whom God spared and did not punish as soon as they sinned, even though he knew that they would not repent or turn to him, because their seed was evil from the beginning. So do not say, "If I were not acting well, God would certainly never have spared me," when you see that your partners in crime were given room for repentance for a long time, so that they might at last see the causes of their evil deeds and make satisfaction to God for their offense. You too, then, unless you are converted to God, will be one of that accursed race of which it is said to God: "knowing well that their nation is wicked and their malice inborn, and that their way of thinking could never change; for they were a seed accursed from the beginning." How glorious will you think yourself, then, when you begin to be with such people, when you see yourself judged among them, when you are found among them and cast into unquenchable flames? Surely you will be first of all, and greater even there, in those punishments. For no one could be found to equal you in wickedness except the devil alone, so that anyone else in those punishments will be seen to be better than you. You dare to say: "If I were not living well, if my works were not right, if my faith, that is, the Arian faith, were not catholic, if I had not done right in removing those bishops who preach the faith set down by the three hundred and more at Nicaea, I would never be reigning so long, I would never shine so brightly in my kingdom that, even if only for a short time, I ruled alone within the Roman frontier." If it is as you say, why does Job, that most righteous worshipper of God, say to those who were assailing his righteousness with false charges: "Hear me, since the pains of my wound compel me to speak. Why do the ungodly live, and their houses are not ruined, and fear is far from them? Their cow has never miscarried, but has always carried her calf to term. They themselves endure like sheep forever, and their children take up the instrument and play with delight, so that they spend their life in good things, though the Lord says: Depart from me, you wicked; I do not want to know your ways. For the lamp of the ungodly will be put out, and they will grieve with groaning in their life. They will be like chaff carried off by the wind, or like dust whirled about by a storm; let their eyes see death. Since I know that the Lord has said these things of them, know that none of you can restrain me and keep me silent." Why does the most glorious Job say this? Only because he knew that very many people do evil and yet are not requited at once [?], but are kept for this purpose: that they either correct themselves or else, after death, feel the penalties of their offenses, and feel what it meant not to have sought God, not to have served him while there was opportunity, and not to have won his favor by believing in him alone and serving him. Now, I believe, convicted by the testimony of so great a man, you will stop saying that you acted justly in removing the Lord's priests, ordaining men of the Arian faith, and ordering the faith of the Arian doctrine to be preached, and in proscribing, deporting, torturing, and killing those who believe in the only Son of God. You will stop saying, I say, that you live and flourish so in your kingdom because you did and are still doing those things, when you hear the righteous man Job, whom God said had served him blamelessly and whom he called his true worshipper, saying that very many people act ungodly and yet live most pleasantly in this life. Deign further to receive what he says below about you ungodly people, and learn how, though you act wickedly, you are being spared for the time being; and present yourself to God through repentance. "I did not know that such darkness would come before my face. Why then, Lord, could I not hide for a single hour? But the ungodly cross into the borders of others; they have seized flocks of sheep together with their shepherds, they have afflicted the cattle of orphans, and taken the widow's ox in pledge. They have reaped a field not their own before its time, and forced men to work in their vineyards without pay. They have plundered many and taken bread from the hungry; they have lain in wait in many narrow passes, and have not understood the way of righteousness. Cursed be their portion on earth. For what hope do ungodly men have, or what access can they have to the Lord? Even if they grow strong, they will come to want, and those of them who are left will die an evil death, and no one will pity their widows. And if they heap up gold or silver like mud, the righteous will possess all of it." So do not see fit any longer to flatter yourself without cause, emperor, for you are just as we have declared, or to suppose that you, a murderer and a sacrilegious man, have lived so very long in this life because your works are acceptable to God. Your works are like the works of those against whom the Holy Spirit inveighs by the mouth of Isaiah, saying: "Thus says the Lord who delivered you, the Holy One of Israel: I am God; I have shown you the way in which you should walk. If you had listened to my commandments, your peace would have been like a river and your righteousness like the waves of the sea, and your offspring would have been like the sand of the sea, and the children of your womb."

But, you say, these words were spoken to the Jews; yes, to the very people whose imitator you have made yourself. And now, as has often been said, change your wicked ways, believe as the holy Church believes, and he will be gracious to you in all things. For he himself says: “Return to me with your whole heart, with fasting and weeping and mourning; rend your hearts and not your garments.” Return to God with your whole heart. Accept these healing remedies so that you may come to understand your crime. Open the eyes of your heart, and as you realize how grievously you have sinned, groan with your whole heart. Then he will have mercy on you who says: “When you have turned and groaned, then you will be saved, and you will know where you have been.” Remember that the prophet consecrated to God said: “I do not desire the death of the one who is dying, says the Lord, so much as that he should turn back and live.” Stop supposing, then, that you are acting rightly because you have not at once paid the penalty for your deeds, even though your works are evil. Look instead at what is written: the Lord is patient, so that you may repent. “Do not say: I have sinned, and what harm has come to me? For the Most High is a patient repayer.” Listen also to the blessed Paul as he invites you to God and makes clear to you how God may be appeased toward you. He shows that God is patient, and that what your works deserve has not been paid out to you at once, because he wants you at last to rise out of your evil through repentance, through true satisfaction: “Or do you despise the riches of his goodness and patience, not knowing that the goodness of God is leading you to repentance? But by your hardness and impenitent heart you are storing up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and of the revelation of the just judgment of God, who will repay each one according to his works.” Return to God, Constantius. Take up the weapons of repentance against the robbery of your inner enemy. Flee the ruinous praise of flatterers, who have not deigned to tell you what they really think. Remember that the Lord said through the mouth of Isaiah: “Those who call you happy lead you into error and confuse the path of your feet.” Believe in the only Son of God and receive pardon for your crimes. Repeat the words of the psalmist: “Who will confess to you in the underworld?” And again: “Will the dust make confession to you?” Return to God and groan over your crimes. Hear the voice of the Lord speaking through Jeremiah: “Does not one who falls rise again, or one who turns away turn back?” You fell on the day you denied the Son of God; you will rise in the hour you confess him. Because the enemy’s blow has struck you, hand yourself over to the physician to be cured; apply the remedy to yourself. You wounded yourself by saying, “He is not the true Son of God”; you will heal yourself again if you say, as we say and believe, that he is the true Son of God. “Return,” says Joel, “to the Lord your God, for he is merciful and kind and patient and abounding in compassion, and he turns back the sentence of evil he has imposed.” If you decide to reject this pardon promised to you for the deaths you have caused, you will long to obtain it in that place where you will receive nothing but the torments of punishment.
